items.title: 60499_Garvin Bushell oral history interview
items.q: He had on bass -- he had Pop Foster on bass... But it was an all New York band.

ctx.x: Now, what year was this about?

This must have been '46, yeah. And I played this concert with him and he liked the way I played clarinet and I played another date with him, and he decided he had this album to make and he wanted me to play that album with him. He used all New York musicians -- Don Kirkpatrick on piano was a New Yorker, and he also used Ed Cuffy who was a trumbone player, he was in New York -- Cuffy was from the mid-west but he lived in New York for many years. He had on bass -- he had Pop Foster on bass, and drums -- who was on…

Carnegie Hall. We recorded it in Carnegie Hall and we went into Carnegie Hall at 12:00 o'clock -- oh, (Well upon) Wilman Braud was the base player, not Pop Foster, Broe. William Braud, that's the name -- he's from New Orleans. And we went in at 12:00 o'clock and it just began to snow. When we came out at 5:00 that evening the busses were straddling the roads. There was snow, I think, three feet deep. That's how hard it had snowed in New York while we were recording. I remember Bunk saying -- he'd never seen snow,…
